content:
marie: heads up — over the last 10m we're seeing a big spike in retries and client-side timeouts to model-svc in us-west-2 (dedicated gpu pool). CPU on pods is fine but request latencies jump and traffic is uneven across endpoints

jason: any packet loss on the nodes? retry patterns look like one backend gets hammered then connections drop

marie: good call, i pulled `ipvsadm -Ln --stats` on a node and it shows extremely lopsided packet counts. also saw a lot of retransmits in kube-proxy logs

alex: can you paste the ipvs output?

marie: sure — snippet:
```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.10.100.25:8080 rr
  -> 172.31.8.5:8080               Masq    1      23000       12
  -> 172.31.9.7:8080               Masq    1       3000       10
  -> 172.31.10.12:8080             Masq    1       2000       14

Totals: packets 1,200,000  bytes 120G
```

jason: that's extreme — 172.31.8.5 has 7x the load of others. Could be hash imbalance, conntrack skew, or a sticky NAT issue

alex: what NIC stats look like? `ethtool -S eth0` and `dmesg` for any XDP/RDMA warnings

marie: `ethtool -S` shows rx_errors and rx_no_buf spikes on the busy host. dmesg had `NETDEV WATCHDOG` and some TCP aborts.

tasha: ping/mtu test between pods on different node pools? we had an MTU mismatch last quarter where some gpu nodes were 9000 and others 1500, that created fragmentation and caused weird ipvs fallback behavior

marie: running `ping -M do -s 8972` between replicas — fragmentation fails from the overloaded backend to some peers. looks like that exact mismatch: gpu-pool A MTU 9000, gpu-pool B 1500 (weirdly the windows-intel pool got defaulted)

jason: aha. path MTU causes packets to be fragmented or dropped; IPVS may keep connections to the node that can accept jumbo frames leading to imbalance. also kernel offload differences can amplify load on one node

alex: quick mitigation: mark the affected node pool to drain incoming service traffic with a `kubectl label node <node> ipvs-drain=true` and add an `externalTrafficPolicy` or use `kubectl patch` to adjust service `sessionAffinity` temporarily. But draining is safer if it's actually dropping packets

marie: doing a rolling cordon+drain on the single bad host now. also setting MTU to 1500 on the gpu-pool A SR-IOV interfaces as a follow-up so all node pools align

net-oncall-bot: noticed route metric change on node 172.31.8.5 at 2027-10-04T15:37:12Z — interface eth1 flapped (ifdown)

tasha: we'll need a postmortem runbook entry — add checks: `ipvsadm --stats`, `ethtool -S`, `ip route show`, `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` and a quick MTU map for node pools. Also maybe add an alert for large ipvs packet skew (per-service imbalance > 4x across endpoints)

jason: agree — adding a short playbook. long-term we should: align MTUs across node pools, enable consistent NIC driver versions, and add a kube-proxy config validation that flags SR-IOV/jumbo combos.

marie: mitigation complete — drain finished, traffic rebalanced, retries dropping back to normal. scheduling a follow-up to fix MTU on the affected pool and a runbook PR. :thumbsup:

alex: nice work. can we also capture `ipvsadm -Ln --stats` snapshot into the incident ticket? helps for future heuristics

marie: done, uploaded to incident ticket #INC-4537. will post the runbook link once PR lands.
